evidence: create-product-dto.ts: CreateProductDto only uses @IsString/@IsNumber shape checks; its doc comment says the Name and Price rules stay in the domain validators
create-product.command.ts: CreateProductCommand(product: CreateProductDto) just copies name/description/price, with no rules of its own
create-product.service.ts: CreateProductService.execute builds new CreateProductCommand(dto) and sends it with commandBus.execute, so the handler is never called directly

create-product.command-handler.ts: CreateProductCommandHandler.execute calls Product.create(Name.create, Description.create, Price.create), then checks product.isValid / product.brokenRules.getBrokenRules() and throws BrokenRulesException, so the rules are not duplicated
All four files are re-exported together from create-product/index.ts, and the controller depends only on CreateProductService
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All four files serve one concern, the create-product use case, and together they form one CQRS pipeline. CreateProductService turns the DTO into a CreateProductCommand and sends it through the CommandBus. CreateProductCommand copies the DTO's fields. CreateProductCommandHandler builds the aggregate from the shared value objects, checks the aggregate's own validity state, saves the product and publishes its events.

Validation rules are kept in one place. The DTO checks only the shape of the input (fields present, right types). The domain rules (Name length, positive Price) stay in the value objects and the aggregate, and the handler reads them back through product.isValid / brokenRules instead of re-checking them itself.

Each file uses the module's own abstractions. The service always goes through the command bus and never calls the handler directly, and the handler always creates the product with Product.create.

The handler injects the concrete ProductRepository from the infrastructure folder. That is a layer-dependency question, which is checked by other tools and is out of scope here.
